title: Trump and Rodríguez Hold First-Ever Face-to-Face Meeting at UN General Assembly
detail: President Trump and Venezuelan interim President Delcy Rodríguez met in person for the first time on September 23, an informal pull-aside during a reception Trump hosted on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York — Rodríguez's first visit to the United States since taking office. She was accompanied by Foreign Minister Félix Plasencia; Trump was joined by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Chief of Staff Susie Wiles and Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller. Rodríguez said the two discussed 'strengthening the bilateral relationship between our countries and moving forward with a cooperation agenda in strategic areas such as energy, mining, and security,' as well as restructuring Venezuela's sovereign debt, and called the encounter 'historic' in a post on X. It was the first meeting between the two leaders since US forces captured Nicolás Maduro in the January 2026 raid.

media.caption: Trump and Rodríguez met on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, their first-ever face-to-face meeting

title: María Corina Machado Makes Three More Failed Attempts to Return to Venezuela
detail: Opposition leader María Corina Machado tried three separate times within 24 hours to re-enter Venezuela — first by boat, then a flight toward Aruba, then another air route toward Curaçao (with Bonaire also considered) — bringing her total to seven failed attempts since she left the country in December 2025 to receive the Nobel Peace Prize in Norway. Adviser Pedro Urruchurtu said 'they are not allowing her to return to her own country,' describing 'three attempts, by maritime and air routes, from Panama, without success'; journalist Idania Chirinos reported authorities canceled the initial boat trip, citing 'mechanical problems.' The attempts coincided with Rodríguez's trip to New York for the UN General Assembly and meeting with Trump. Machado's team said she is planning a public return with supporters coordinating civilian security, as part of a broader plan to tour Venezuela's 23 states and press for a new presidential election. The US State Department has publicly recognized her right to return.

media.caption: María Corina Machado attempted three routes back into Venezuela in 24 hours as Rodríguez met Trump in New York
